notes: Complex-query focus. Both configs produced the correct final answer on all 3 evals (eval 9: 10 gold rows; eval 10: 7 gold rows; eval 11: 539/3164/ANG OUSA/156).

with_skill 16/17 assertions, baseline 17/17. The single with_skill miss: eval 9 inlined 'hard' and the datetime as string literals in the filter template instead of filter_params - breaking the skill's OWN 'never string interpolation' rule. Baseline, with no such rule, parametrized cleanly. Under complex-filter load the rule did not stick because the skill shows no relation-traversal / multi-condition templating example.

The skill provides ~no lift on PocketBase filter SYNTAX - Sonnet already handles relation traversal (challenge.difficulty), parenthesised ||/&& groups, date-string comparison, and compound sort (-score,name) unaided.

Both configs independently hit the same friction the skill does not cover: (a) fields projection without 'id' -> ~200 pydantic validation errors on fetch_all; (b) expand + fetch_all ignores projection on expanded rows -> 90KB-450KB dumps; (c) per_page is silently capped near 1000; (d) relation whose id equals its slug (category='web') vs needing a lookup - agents burned 2-3 calls guessing; (e) no GROUP BY, and a pre-aggregated view (_submission_stats) existed but was found only after doing it the hard way.

eval 11 cost: with_skill 19 calls / 101s / 54k tok; baseline 27 calls / 209s / 73k tok. Directionally the skill's inspect-first habit trimmed flailing, but n=1 and both overflowed context on the big fetch.

Actionable: add a 'Complex queries' section with a worked relation-traversal + compound-filter example (all values parametrized), the operator table, and a 'large / grouped results' subsection covering id-in-projection, expand size, per_page cap, client-side tally, and checking for a view first.
